extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, and patent attorneys/agents filing or prosecuting patents in Brazil (INPI)
extracted.subtask_short: filing and prosecuting patents in Brazil
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and procedural requirements for entering the national phase, requesting examination, using the PPH, filing divisionals, paying grant/maintenance fees, and required translations when prosecuting patent applications before the Brazilian Patent Office (INPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The national phase deadline with the Brazilian Patent Office (INPI) is 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of the title, claims, and abstract must be submitted at the 30-month deadline in Brazil. Applicants may file an extension for the Portuguese specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirements and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation of the title, claims, and abstract must be submitted at the 30-month deadline; extension for the Portuguese specification is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit translated title, claims and abstract at 30 months. If additional time is needed for the full Portuguese specification, an extension may be filed (the page explicitly notes applicants may file an extension for the Portuguese specification).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH (Patent Prosecution Highway) eligibility and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedural conditions for requesting participation in the PPH in Brazil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points listed on the page: - No fixed deadline to request PPH in Brazil, but the application must have been published (or an anticipated publication requested). - The technical examination must have been requested (but not yet initiated by the BRPTO for PPH purposes — initiation occurs when an office action, unfavorable opinion, or grant publication happens). - Application must have been filed for at least 18 months or have a request for anticipated publication, or (for international applications) been published by WIPO. - No divisional or voluntary amendments may be made between PPH request submission and its decision (divisional filings must be done before the PPH request; the PPH request is possible for either parent or divisional individually). - The application must belong to a patent family with at least an older patent application filed with INPI or an Office of Earlier Examination. - The family must include an Office of Earlier Examination that has examined the family and considered subject matter patentable in a substantive examination, or that has issued a decision of approval/grant. - Claims submitted must be equal to or more restricted than the subject matter considered patentable by the Office of Earlier Examination; inclusion of matter not searched/examined by the Office of Earlier Examination is prohibited even if the claim is restricted. - Provide the required supportive documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Original claims should be filed first; amended claims can be filed later in conjunction with a request for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the original set of claims prior to an amended set is recommended; amended claims can be submitted later when filing the request for examination to defer an additional fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for substantive (technical) examination must be filed within three years from the international filing date of the PCT application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible to request accelerated examination under the PPH program. Ensure the substantive examination request is timely (within the three-year limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional filing timing and content limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope and timing constraints for filing divisional patent applications in Brazil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Brazil, divisionals are limited to what is presented in the claims filed when the application starts examination. Best practice: retain the entire claim chapter (do not delete claims) until the Brazilian Office decides on patentability and any lack-of-unity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant fee and maintenance (renewal) fee deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for paying grant and annual (maintenance) fees in Brazil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant fees are due 60 days from the issuance of the Notice of Allowance. Maintenance (annual) fees apply to pending applications and are due on the anniversary of the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brazilian patent official fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: List of official fees (USD) associated with filing, examination, extensions, reinstatement, issue, and annual maintenance in Brazil as listed on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees shown on the page: - Official Filing fee: $35 (USD) - Official Examination fee: $325 (USD) - Official Examination fee (up to 10 claims): $115 (USD) - Official Examination fee (each claim 11-15): $20 (USD) - Official Examination fee (each claim 16-30): $40 (USD) - Official Examination fee (each claim in excess of 30): $100 (USD) - Official Extension fee: $165 (USD) - Official Reinstatement fee: $20 (USD) - Official Issue fee: $125 (USD) - Official Annual fees (pending applications): $60 (USD) - Official Annual fees (1-2): $60 (USD) - Official Annual fees (3-6): $150 (USD) - Official Annual fees (7-10): $230 (USD) - Official Annual fees (11-15): $310 (USD) - Official Annual fees (16-20): $380 (USD)
